The prechecks' standing-destination guard backs a rare clash. Tested: an open test sprint t.md beside a closed t.md takes t-3.md (t-2.md taken by the plan), and t-plan.json takes t-plan-2.json.

fields.choice: companions hold only the unsuffixed name, and a suffix opening with a number is no companion

body: resolve runs before the first apply (ADMINISTRATION: resolve then true-up again), and retire_rule_file archives there. body: move_all records archived entries before a conversion's moves, and move_back keeps them (the ledger only appends). The next true-up's intake_migration_refusals then refuses the same conversion: 'the closed-record ledger already lists <names> under .ok-planner/history/issues/', and no verb clears a ledger entry, so a conversion whose import failed after the dry run cannot run again. Options: (a) keep, as built: the failure is rare, since the dry run in prechecks catches most refusals; (b) record the conversion's entries after the import succeeds, departing from bookkeeping-before-the-move for a step that undoes its own moves; (c) let a conversion reuse a held name whose file does not stand while its source does, with record_archived skipping names already listed.
